metric.semantic_density.methodology: Raw value = (count of frozen site_id rows whose evidence state is EXPLICIT_LOCAL, summed over all measured Java fragments) / (lexical source tokens of those fragments, summed). Tokens counted with a language-neutral whitespace+punctuation split consistent with the frozen tokenizer intent in semantic_compression.md sec 6.1.3 (identifiers, keywords, literals, operators, and each punctuation mark each count as one token; comments/whitespace excluded). Facts drawn only from the frozen site_id rows in semantic_site_matrix.json for each probe; only EXPLICIT_LOCAL rows enter the numerator per the frozen counting rule. NONLOCAL/IMPLICIT/ABSENT rows are recorded but excluded from the density numerator (they feed Locality/Hidden-Cost metrics computed by other workers).

none_probes.reason: N-4/N-1: Java has no documented mechanism for two names in the same scope to denote the same primitive scalar local storage with write access (no pointers/refs to locals; only object references to heap objects). Per canonical_task and support rubric N-4, no fragment written.

N-1/N-4: Java has no documented way for a callee to write a caller's scalar local variable; wrapping the int in a mutable container is explicitly disallowed as a FULL substitute by the probe's own rubric text. No fragment written.

N-1: Standard javac/java frozen recipe (no --enable-preview / --add-modules incubator flags) does not expose a finalized, non-preview built-in FFI mechanism reaching libc abs(int) without such flags, which would be a P-b deviation outside the frozen recipe. No fragment written.

N-1: javac/java produce JVM bytecode (.class/.jar), not a native compiled artifact with an `nm`-visible unmangled exported C symbol, under the frozen recipe. nm evidence: 'no compiled artifact under the frozen recipe'.

normalization_applied.method: PROVISIONAL single-language linear transform: score = min(100, round(raw_density * 1000)). This worker was assigned only Java and has no visibility into the other nine languages' raw densities, so no genuine cross-language min-max or common-basis normalization is possible in this shard. Per capability_universe.json 'interaction_with_quality_metrics', metrics A-D are properly computed on a COMMON BASIS across all ten languages; the runner must recompute the final normalized Semantic Density score for Java (and all languages) once every language shard's raw per-probe counts are merged, restricting to the common basis (probes where all ten languages have a fragment) and applying the run's frozen cross-language normalization rule.

partial_probes.reason: Java arrays are always zero/default-initialized; no documented way to obtain genuinely uninitialized bulk storage. Substituted the default-initialized byte[16] per R9.
No standard checked/wrapping/saturating op for int addition in java.lang.Math beyond Math.addExact (throws, not optional-valued); used rung (iv) plain '+' which silently wraps.
No standard optional-returning integer division in the JDK; used rung (ii) explicit local guard on b==0.
No standard optional-returning narrowing conversion in the JDK; used rung (ii) explicit (int) cast, which truncates silently.
